title: Engineer security into design decisions: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: How do design principles constrain a proposed failure path before implementation?
focalInsight: Secure architecture links each principle to a trust boundary and a specific unsafe state.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Secure Design
nodes.definition: Deliberate architecture that reduces exploitable failure paths before deployment.
nodes.detail: Deliberate architecture that reduces exploitable failure paths before deployment.
nodes.decision: Use when a requirement must survive change, misuse, or component failure.
nodes.failureExample: A feature works in normal testing but has no defined behavior when its authorization service fails.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Design the allowed and denied state before selecting the feature.

nodes.label: Least Privilege
nodes.definition: Grant only authority necessary for a defined task and duration.
nodes.detail: Grant only authority necessary for a defined task and duration.
nodes.decision: Scope each human, service, and admin role to its required action.
nodes.failureExample: One deployment account can read every production secret.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Remove unnecessary permissions; broad convenience creates blast radius.

nodes.label: Defense In Depth
nodes.definition: Independent safeguards arranged so one failed control does not expose the asset.
nodes.detail: Independent safeguards arranged so one failed control does not expose the asset.
nodes.decision: Choose layers with different failure modes across identity, network, endpoint, and recovery.
nodes.failureExample: A stolen password reaches sensitive data because no second control checks device or action.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A stack is defense in depth only if failures are not common-mode.

nodes.label: Secure Defaults
nodes.definition: Initial configuration that protects the asset without requiring a user to opt in.
nodes.detail: Initial configuration that protects the asset without requiring a user to opt in.
nodes.decision: Choose the safe initial state when setup is incomplete or ambiguous.
nodes.failureExample: A new storage bucket is publicly readable until an owner changes a setting.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Start closed and deliberately grant the exception.

nodes.label: Fail Securely
nodes.definition: Behavior that denies or limits unsafe action when a security decision cannot be made.
nodes.detail: Behavior that denies or limits unsafe action when a security decision cannot be made.
nodes.decision: Define the safe state for dependency loss, timeout, or malformed input.
nodes.failureExample: An authorization timeout causes a gateway to allow the request.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: If the security decision is unavailable, do not silently authorize.

nodes.label: Separation Of Duties
nodes.definition: Division of conflicting authority so one role cannot complete a sensitive action alone.
nodes.detail: Division of conflicting authority so one role cannot complete a sensitive action alone.
nodes.decision: Separate request, approval, implementation, and review where fraud or error matters.
nodes.failureExample: The same administrator requests, deploys, and approves a payment-rule change.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Independent approval reduces unchecked conflicting power.

nodes.label: Zero Trust
nodes.definition: Access approach that evaluates identity, device, context, and request instead of trusting network location.
nodes.detail: Access approach that evaluates identity, device, context, and request instead of trusting network location.
nodes.decision: Re-evaluate access at a meaningful request or session boundary.
nodes.failureExample: An internal subnet lets a compromised workstation call an admin API.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Internal location is a signal, not proof of authorized action.

nodes.label: Privacy By Design
nodes.definition: Design practice that makes purpose, minimization, and accountability part of the system.
nodes.detail: Design practice that makes purpose, minimization, and accountability part of the system.
nodes.decision: Ask what personal data is needed for the stated purpose and lifecycle.
nodes.failureExample: A feature collects precise location forever for a one-time delivery estimate.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Collect and retain only what the purpose requires.

nodes.label: Shared Responsibility
nodes.definition: Explicit allocation of security operation and assurance duties among parties.
nodes.detail: Explicit allocation of security operation and assurance duties among parties.
nodes.decision: Map every layer and control to an accountable operator and verifier.
nodes.failureExample: A customer assumes a provider configured tenant sharing and alerting.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Provider capability does not establish customer configuration or accountability.
